transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ben (Redwood CSM), Jordan (CTO - Zetta), Maya (Head of ML), Diego (Infra), Talia (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Discussed upcoming holiday traffic, capacity options, canary plan for model v2, ask for pilot pricing and security checklist.

[00:00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off in a sec. Appreciate you all making time.
[00:00:08] Jordan Park: Yeah thanks Alex, we got the agenda, excited to get into the capacity bits — holiday sprint is coming up.
[00:00:15] Priya Rao: Quick note, I'll share my screen in a moment to show the baseline metrics and the recommended Dedicated pockets + fallback policies.
[00:00:23] Maya Singh: Awesome. High level for us: we need to keep 95th percentile latency under 250ms for the checkout flow, cost target is, um, roughly 20% less than our current self-hosted outlay.
[00:00:36] Diego Ruiz: Quick interruption — is that 250ms end-to-end or just inference?
[00:00:00] (speaker overlap) Maya Singh: inference, yeah inference only. Application and network add about 40-60ms on our side.
[00:00:55] Priya Rao: Great, so our suggestion is a hybrid: Dedicated pools for high-throughput checkout endpoints, hosted for lower-priority background clips. We'll route by route, low-latency SLOs pinned to Dedicated.
[00:01:10] Talia - Product Manager: When you say "route by route" can you clarify operationally what that looks like? Do we need separate endpoints?
[00:01:18] Priya Rao: Good q. You can keep the same API surface, we handle routing at the control plane — you tag routes with SLO and cost tier, Redwood will direct traffic to Dedicated or Hosted based on the policy. There's an option for automatic fallback if Dedicated is saturated.
[00:01:35] Jordan Park: And fallback means it could go to a cheaper, higher latency hosted model? I need to understand customer-visible behavior.
[00:01:42] Priya Rao: Yes. We can configure fallback to either queue, return a degraded but acceptable model, or fail closed. You can pick per-route policy. For checkout we recommend fail open to a smaller model variant with a controlled confidence threshold.
[00:02:00] Alex Mercer: Quick commercial note — Dedicated pools are reservable; we can provision burst capacity but that costs more. We'll put numbers in the pilot pricing sheet.
[00:02:10] Jordan Park: Can you ballpark now? We need an order of magnitude to make decisions for Q4 budget.
[00:02:15] Ben Cho: Ballpark: for the profile you shared (30 qps steady, 200 p95 tokens) a modest Dedicated commit buys predictable latency and is usually 30-40% more cost than hosted per token, but yields 2-3x lower p95 latency. Exact depends on quantization and sequence lengths.
[00:02:36] Maya Singh: 30-40% more... that's significant. We need to balance. Could quantization close that gap?
[00:02:43] Priya Rao: Quantization helps — we recommend int8 for these models; goes a long way. Also batching and prefix caching for chatty flows. For checkout though, batching isn't great because of latency sensitivity.
[00:02:58] Diego Ruiz: On the technical side — what's the memory footprint for your Dedicated variant vs hosted? We have constrained GPU counts in our holiday region.
[00:03:06] Priya Rao: Dedicated uses same model variant, but we can offer a quantized 8-bit variant that reduces GPU vram by ~30%. There's also a sharded option for very long contexts.
[00:03:18] Jordan Park: You mentioned automatic prefix caching — does that require us to modify prompts or store any tokens? Data residency concerns here.
[00:03:26] Priya Rao: Good call. Prefix/KV caching is optional, and we can scope cache lifetime and storage location. For Private deployments we can keep cache inside the V P C. For hosted it'll be in Redwood's encrypted cache — we can share SOC2 artifacts.
[00:03:42] Talia: I want to flag security — procurement wants SSO, SAML, and audit logs preserved for model calls. Are those available?
[00:03:50] Alex Mercer: Yes, SSO/SAML and token-level audit logs are supported. We'll attach security docs and the SOC2 summary.
[00:03:56] Jordan Park: Ok please do. Also are there region residency constraints? We need EU only for some customers.
[00:04:02] Priya Rao: We have region pinning and Private option. For EU-only traffic, we recommend Redwood Private in a customer VPC in the EU region — that meets data residency and KMS control needs.
[00:04:15] Maya Singh: For the canary rollout of model v2, we want deterministic rollback triggers. What metrics do you watch?
[00:04:22] Priya Rao: We monitor latency, error rate, and quality regressions against a prompt set. Redwood's Optimize toolkit can run automated evaluation on a prompt bank; if quality dips beyond set threshold we pause the rollout and automatically fallback.
[00:04:37] Maya Singh: Is Optimize able to run offline evaluations or does it run on live traffic? We want to avoid leaking production data into evals.
[00:04:44] Priya Rao: You can upload a curated prompt set (recommended) for offline evals; we also have optional live A/B that uses synthetic identifiers so PII isn't stored. We'll send docs on best practices.
[00:04:59] Diego Ruiz: Network note — V P C peering with your control plane, what's the handshake? We prefer customer-initiated peering and own the tunnel keys.
[00:05:06] Priya Rao: Ok, that's supported. We do both normal VPN and private-link style peering. We'll detail requirements.
[00:05:12] Jordan Park: Let's get into the 2-week benchmark plan. We want numbers so finance can sign.
[00:05:18] Alex Mercer: Proposed benchmark: 2 weeks of synthetic traffic that matches your expected QPS and sequence lengths. We'll run Dedicated commit + hosted fallback scenario and report p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and unit cost per 1k tokens.
[00:05:33] Maya Singh: Can you include tail-latency breakdown by model stage (tokenization, attention, KV cache miss)? We need to know where optimizations will matter.
[00:05:41] Priya Rao: We'll capture breakdowns as best as instrumentation allows; attention kernels are usually the heavy hitter for long contexts. If you send representative prompts we'll align the trace points.
[00:05:52] (crosstalk) Diego Ruiz: Also, if we run into throttling during holiday ramp, how graceful is your autoscale?
[00:05:58] Ben Cho: Autoscale can be configured per-pool. Dedicated autoscale is based on commit headroom — you can set burst thresholds. When burst capacity is exceeded, fallback policies kick in. We can simulate ramp to validate.
[00:06:12] Talia: On rollouts — we need explicit rollback criteria written into the runbook. Can Redwood provide a sample runbook?
[00:06:19] Priya Rao: Yes, Priya: will share the canary runbook template after the call.
[00:06:24] Alex Mercer: (laughs) that's Priya's lane.
[00:06:27] Priya Rao: Yup, sending after.
[00:06:30] Jordan Park: Pricing again — if Dedicated is 30-40% more, but gives us latency guarantees, would a smaller Dedicated pool + more aggressive fallback be cheaper overall?
[00:06:39] Ben Cho: Potentially. A hybrid mix often reduces overall burn while protecting the most-critical endpoints. That's why per-route tagging and cost routing is helpful. We'll model a 2-pool scenario in the spreadsheet.
[00:06:50] Maya Singh: We have a constraint: legal wants no model outputs saved to external buckets for checkout logs. Can you do no retention?
[00:06:58] Priya Rao: Yes, retention is configurable. You can set zero retention and still capture token-level billing metrics without storing text. We'll document the options.
[00:07:08] Diego Ruiz: Any integration work for our infra team? We use a homegrown gateway, not Envoy.
[00:07:14] Priya Rao: Standard REST + SDKs work. For advanced routing you'll add a header to tag routes and SLO selection is via the control plane API. We'll provide example snippets for a generic gateway.
[00:07:27] Jordan Park: Competitors question — we've demoed OtherCloudAI which promised cheaper burst pricing. Why would we pick Redwood?
[00:07:34] Alex Mercer: Two reasons: predictable SLOs and operational tooling for rollouts & quality monitoring. Others are cheaper sometimes but lack quality guardrails and route-level controls — that introduces risk during high-traffic events.
[00:07:47] Maya Singh: Noted.
[00:07:49] (long pause)
[00:08:05] Alex Mercer: Ok turning to timeline — we propose: Redwood sends pilot config + pricing by 2027-10-05. Zetta approves pilot scope by 2027-10-07. Start bench 2027-10-10 for two weeks. Post-benchmark decision meeting 2027-10-24 to finalize commit.
[00:08:20] Talia: That timeline works for product and finance if we get the sheet.
[00:08:24] Jordan Park: One more thing — will you support emergency on-call during holiday ramp?
[00:08:30] Ben Cho: Yes we offer a premium on-call add-on with 24/7 pager duty support for Dedicated customers during critical windows. We'll include pricing.
[00:08:40] Maya Singh: Great.
[00:08:42] Diego Ruiz: Quick nitpick — you used the term "KV cache miss" earlier, your transcript docs spelled it "K V cash miss" sometimes. just, you know, minor.
[00:08:52] Priya Rao: (laughs) the auto transcript does that a lot.
[00:08:56] Alex Mercer: Alright, we'll wrap with action items. Ben, can you recap the commercial asks?
[00:09:02] Ben Cho: Sure: I'll prepare the pilot pricing spreadsheet with two scenarios (small Dedicated commit + hybrid fallback; larger Dedicated commit with burst) and include unit cost, expected p95 impact, and SLA language.
[00:09:13] Alex Mercer: Priya will send the canary runbook and benchmark checklist. I'll send the SOC2 excerpt and sample pilot contract language.
[00:09:21] Priya Rao: Sending links right after.
[00:09:24] Jordan Park: Diego will validate peering and network needs. Maya will provide prompt sets. Talia will coordinate finance.
[00:09:31] (short silence)
[00:09:40] Alex Mercer: Anything else?
[00:09:42] Talia: No, that's it. Thanks.
[00:09:44] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:46] (call ends and people start leaving)

Post-call notes (auto):
- Redwood to share pilot config + pricing spreadsheet (Ben/Alex).
- Priya to share canary runbook and benchmark checklist.
- Zetta to validate VPC peering and surface network contacts.
- Two-week synthetic benchmark scheduled to start 2027-10-10.

Questions raised during call:
- How is fallback handled for user-visible checkout flows? (answered: configurable per-route, can fail to smaller model variant)
- Is prefix/KV caching compatible with data residency constraints? (answered: yes, can be VPC-scoped or disabled)
- What triggers automatic rollback during canary? (answered: latency/error/quality thresholds tied to prompt bank)

Notes on transcript quality: medium — several product names and acronyms mistranscribed (e.g., "K V cash", "V P C").
